title: HogEye vs. Spartan GoLive for Hog Traps
reader_sentence: A Spartan GoLive will show you live video, but on a hog trap the question is whether you can close the gate from that same screen when the last hog walks in, so check that before you put any camera on your trap.

evidence.signal: spartan golive 260/mo (390-480 Oct-Nov), spartan golive 2 110, spartan camera 6,600 (12,100 Oct-Nov)

key_points: Spartan sells the GoLive 3 as a cellular scouting camera. It sends 8MP photos and 60-second HD video with sound to your phone, and it can live stream.
The Spartan GoLive 3 is $289.95 to $299.95 depending on camo, on Verizon or AT&T, from Spartan's store.
The GoLive 3 has a 96-degree field of view, motion detection out to 80 feet, no-glow infrared to 60 feet, and a 12V jack for solar or external power.
The Spartan GoLive 2 live streams at up to 30 frames per second.
Spartan's GoLive listings say nothing about connecting the camera to a trap gate or latch.
The HogEye Mini Camera comes with a gate cable and latch adapter that connect it to the trap's gate, so the same app you watch in sends the close command.
Live video from the HogEye Mini Camera is 720p at 10 frames per second with a 140-degree field of view, wide enough to see inside and outside the trap.
You watch the hogs inside and outside the trap in the app, and when the whole sounder is inside you send the close command from your phone and the gate closes.
Closing on part of a sounder teaches the hogs that got away to avoid the trap.
The HogEye Mini Camera is $1,299 on AT&T or Verizon, and the data plan is $49.99 a month with no contract; you can start or stop it anytime.
A scouting camera like the GoLive is useful for finding where hogs are feeding before you set a trap.
notes: Spartan facts from spartancamera.com/products.json (Oct 20, 2026); no plan prices published there, so none are used. Spartan's own copy mentions trespassers; leave that framing out.
